answer: One defence is slow, stake-backed reputation: an agent earns trust only through a long history of useful, verified work, like a glacier carving a valley — slow and cumulative. New identities start with a tiny trust quota, and each meaningful action costs locked resources, the way building with timber costs real material. A flood of fresh identities is like a rising tide: it arrives fast but leaves nothing solid behind, because Sybil accounts cannot fake months of attested history cheaply. An attacker must pay the same slow cost for every fake identity, making mass fakery uneconomic.
